what: Sāriputta, Moggallāna and some 250 of Sañjaya's wanderers
Pūraṇa Kassapa and his teaching of six classes, placed within or beside the Ājīvika order

evidence.detail: AN 6.57 gives Pūraṇa the six classes in which the Ājīvika leaders are supremely white; the Tamil Maṇimēkalai and Nīlakēci make Pūraṇa the Ājīvika teacher.
that Pūraṇa's following merged with the Ājīvikas (metadata only)

what: Pakudha's seven unmade bodies, joined to Ājīvika destiny and the 84 great aeons

evidence.detail: MN 76's fourth negation, SN 24.8's 'great view' and Ja 545's Guṇa combine them; the Tamil Ājīvaka teaches life plus four kinds of eternal atoms.

what: the natthika/uccheda view of the person made of four elements

evidence.detail: DN 2's 'cātumahābhūtiko ayaṃ puriso' and the Bṛhaspati fragments' four elements and 'no other world'
Ajita as forerunner of the Lokāyata (metadata only); no lineage link in the texts

what: the eightfold Mahānimitta, drawn by the six disācaras from the Pūrvas

evidence.detail: Bhagavatī 15 (Jain account — reported by an opponent)

what: a doctrine of six colour-named classes of beings (abhijāti / leśyā)

evidence.detail: the Ājīvika six classes (AN 6.57) and the Jain six leśyās are both six and colour-named; see also brw:vrtra-colours-and-sramana-colour-doctrines (U05)

what: the name Bārhaspatya and a this-worldly view of the sciences

evidence.detail: the Arthaśāstra's Bārhaspatyas (only economics and government; the Veda a cover) and the Lokāyata's 'Bṛhaspati'

what: the refusal of four alternatives and the Jain modes of predication

evidence.detail: some scholars see Sañjaya's formula as a forerunner of the Jain sevenfold predication; the Jain tradition rejects any kinship, classing ajñāna as wrong faith (metadata only).
